findings.title: DNS traffic is being transparently intercepted
findings.detail: A query sent to an address that cannot host a DNS server (TEST-NET / documentation range) received an answer. A router, ISP or security appliance is redirecting all port-53 traffic to its own resolver, so the public resolvers you think you are using are not the ones answering.
evidence: DNS to non-existent server 198.51.100.53: a reply came back from an address that cannot run DNS — port 53 traffic is being transparently intercepted/redirected
DNS to non-existent server 2001:db8::53: no reply (no-ipv6) — no transparent DNS interception detected on this path
findings.recommendation: If it is your own router (e.g. a 'force DNS' / DNS redirect NAT rule, UniFi Content Filtering, Pi-hole interception) this may be intentional. Otherwise use DoH/DoT to bypass, and ask the ISP.

findings.title: Queries to public resolvers are answered by someone else
findings.detail: Several independent checks show that queries addressed to well-known public resolvers are answered by a different system. This is DNS redirection somewhere between this host and the internet.
evidence: System DNS #1 (Google Public DNS) 8.8.8.8:53 returned NXDOMAIN for example.com (a public resolver always resolves it)
System DNS #2 (Google Public DNS) 8.8.4.4:53 returned NXDOMAIN for example.com (a public resolver always resolves it)
Cloudflare primary IPv4 1.1.1.1:53 returned NXDOMAIN for example.com (a public resolver always resolves it)
Quad9 primary IPv4 9.9.9.9:53 returned NXDOMAIN for example.com (a public resolver always resolves it)
OpenDNS (Cisco) primary IPv4 208.67.222.222:53 returned NXDOMAIN for example.com (a public resolver always resolves it)
Control D (free, unfiltered) primary IPv4 76.76.2.0:53 returned NXDOMAIN for example.com (a public resolver always resolves it)
findings.recommendation: Check the router for DNS redirect/'force local DNS' rules. To bypass an ISP-level redirect, use encrypted DNS (DoH/DoT).

findings.title: DNS server 8.8.8.8:53 answers, but not correctly
findings.detail: It responds, yet returned NXDOMAIN for example.com — a name that always exists. The resolver is broken, filtering far too aggressively, or its upstream is failing. Apps will see 'site not found' errors.
evidence: UDP/53 query (A example.com) @ 8.8.8.8:53 — WARN: server answered with NXDOMAIN and no usable address
AAAA query @ 8.8.8.8:53 — WARN: AAAA query returned NXDOMAIN
findings.recommendation: Check the resolver's upstream/forwarder configuration and blocklists; test it against another resolver.

findings.title: Truncated answers cannot be recovered via System DNS #1 (Google Public DNS) (8.8.8.8:53)
findings.detail: large answer could not be fetched over TCP (refused); clients cannot recover from truncated UDP answers
evidence: Truncation → TCP fallback @ 8.8.8.8:53 — FAIL: large answer could not be fetched over TCP (refused); clients cannot recover from truncated UDP answers
findings.recommendation: Allow TCP/53 and check that no middlebox strips the TC flag.

findings.detail: It responds, yet returned NXDOMAIN for example.com — a name that always exists. The resolver is broken, filtering far too aggressively, or its upstream is failing. Apps will see 'site not found' errors.
evidence: UDP/53 query (A example.com) @ 8.8.4.4:53 — WARN: server answered with NXDOMAIN and no usable address
AAAA query @ 8.8.4.4:53 — WARN: AAAA query returned NXDOMAIN
findings.recommendation: Check the resolver's upstream/forwarder configuration and blocklists; test it against another resolver.

findings.recommendation: Allow TCP/53 and check that no middlebox strips the TC flag.

findings.title: Plain HTTP connectivity checks failed
findings.detail: The OS-style connectivity probes could not complete. Devices may report 'No internet'.
evidence: Google (Android/Chrome) http://connectivitycheck.gstatic.com/generate_204 → 0 request failed: Get "http://connectivitycheck.gstatic.com/generate_204": dial tcp: lookup connectivitycheck.gstatic.com on 8.8.8.8:53: no such host (1 ms)

Apple (iOS/macOS) http://captive.apple.com/hotspot-detect.html → 0 request failed: Get "http://captive.apple.com/hotspot-detect.html": dial tcp: lookup captive.apple.com on 8.8.8.8:53: no such host (1 ms)

Microsoft (Windows NCSI) http://www.msftconnecttest.com/connecttest.txt → 0 request failed: Get "http://www.msftconnecttest.com/connecttest.txt": dial tcp: lookup www.msftconnecttest.com on 8.8.8.8:53: no such host (1 ms)
findings.recommendation: Check whether outbound TCP 80 is blocked and that these names resolve.

findings.title: 3 of 4 website tests failed or were unreliable
findings.detail: Other resources loaded, so this is specific to a site, an address family or it is intermittent. A response only counts as loaded when it ends in a complete 2xx answer (redirects are followed; cut-off transfers and error statuses fail).
evidence: https://www.google.com/generate_204: DNS lookup failed: lookup www.google.com on 8.8.8.8:53: no such host
https://www.cloudflare.com/cdn-cgi/trace: DNS lookup failed: lookup www.cloudflare.com on 8.8.8.8:53: no such host
https://www.wikipedia.org/: DNS lookup failed: lookup www.wikipedia.org on 8.8.8.8:53: no such host
github.com IPv4: DNS 1 · connect 0 · TLS 2 · first byte 66 · transfer 0 ms; measured 70 ms end-to-end (1/1 runs ok, range 69–69 ms, HTTP/2.0, 1971 bytes, complete, length verified)
findings.recommendation: Compare which family/site fails; re-run to see whether it is intermittent.

findings.title: Network time (NTP, UDP 123) is unreachable
findings.detail: No NTP server answered. Devices that rely on NTP (routers, IoT, Linux servers, cameras) will drift; large clock errors break TLS, DoT/DoH and DNSSEC.
evidence: time.cloudflare.com (162.159.200.1): no reply on UDP/123 (read udp 192.0.2.2:45150->162.159.200.1:123: read: connection refused)
time.google.com (216.239.35.0): no reply on UDP/123 (read udp 192.0.2.2:36211->216.239.35.0:123: read: connection refused)
findings.recommendation: Allow outbound UDP 123, or point devices at the router's NTP server.

findings.title: Some OS lookups failed (4 of 5)
findings.detail: Name resolution through the OS resolver is intermittent or partially blocked.
evidence: example.com [baseline (A + AAAA)]: lookup example.com on 8.8.8.8:53: no such host (1 ms)
www.google.com [popular dual-stack site]: lookup www.google.com on 8.8.8.8:53: no such host (1 ms)
cloudflare.com [popular dual-stack site]: lookup cloudflare.com on 8.8.8.8:53: no such host (1 ms)
github.com [IPv4-only site]: 140.82.114.3 (23 ms)
ipv6.google.com [IPv6-only name]: lookup ipv6.google.com on 8.8.8.8:53: no such host (1 ms)
www.wikipedia.org [popular dual-stack site]: lookup www.wikipedia.org on 8.8.8.8:53: no such host (1 ms)
localhost [local name (hosts file)]: 127.0.0.1 (1 ms)
sadns-nx-r6s89k7ht9qkyf.com [non-existent name (must fail)]: lookup sadns-nx-r6s89k7ht9qkyf.com on 8.8.8.8:53: no such host (1 ms)
findings.recommendation: Compare the failing names with the per-resolver results.

findings.title: DNS over TCP fails for System DNS #1 (Google Public DNS) (8.8.8.8:53)
findings.detail: Answers that do not fit in UDP (DNSSEC, many TXT/HTTPS records, large CNAME chains) must be retried over TCP. Those lookups will fail.
evidence: TCP/53 query @ 8.8.8.8:53 — WARN: TCP/53 failed (refused) — responses larger than the UDP limit will fail [refused: dial tcp 8.8.8.8:53: connect: connection refused]
findings.recommendation: Allow TCP/53 to the resolver (firewall) and ensure the DNS service listens on TCP.

findings.title: DNS over TCP fails for System DNS #2 (Google Public DNS) (8.8.4.4:53)
findings.detail: Answers that do not fit in UDP (DNSSEC, many TXT/HTTPS records, large CNAME chains) must be retried over TCP. Those lookups will fail.
evidence: TCP/53 query @ 8.8.4.4:53 — WARN: TCP/53 failed (refused) — responses larger than the UDP limit will fail [refused: dial tcp 8.8.4.4:53: connect: connection refused]
findings.recommendation: Allow TCP/53 to the resolver (firewall) and ensure the DNS service listens on TCP.

findings.title: Encrypted DNS (DoT and DoH) does not work
findings.detail: All DNS-over-TLS and DNS-over-HTTPS attempts failed. Either TLS is intercepted, the clock is wrong, or these endpoints are blocked.
findings.recommendation: Check the TLS/clock findings and firewall rules for TCP 853/443 to the resolver IPs.

findings.title: DNS over TCP to the internet is blocked
findings.detail: All 7 reachable public resolvers failed over TCP/53 while UDP worked. A firewall is blocking outbound TCP port 53, which breaks large DNS answers for any resolver outside your network.
findings.recommendation: Allow outbound TCP/53 (at least from your router/local resolver).

findings.title: Modern DNS record types fail via System DNS #1 (Google Public DNS) (8.8.8.8:53)
findings.detail: HTTPS-type query returned NXDOMAIN — Safari, Chrome and iOS request these for every site and may stall or fall back. Apple devices and Chromium query HTTPS records for every site and may stall waiting for them.
evidence: HTTPS/SVCB record type (RFC 9460) @ 8.8.8.8:53 — WARN: HTTPS-type query returned NXDOMAIN — Safari, Chrome and iOS request these for every site and may stall or fall back
findings.recommendation: Update the router firmware or point clients at a resolver that handles all record types (Unbound, AdGuard Home, Pi-hole v6, or a public resolver).

findings.title: Modern DNS record types fail via System DNS #2 (Google Public DNS) (8.8.4.4:53)
findings.detail: HTTPS-type query returned NXDOMAIN — Safari, Chrome and iOS request these for every site and may stall or fall back. Apple devices and Chromium query HTTPS records for every site and may stall waiting for them.
evidence: HTTPS/SVCB record type (RFC 9460) @ 8.8.4.4:53 — WARN: HTTPS-type query returned NXDOMAIN — Safari, Chrome and iOS request these for every site and may stall or fall back
findings.recommendation: Update the router firmware or point clients at a resolver that handles all record types (Unbound, AdGuard Home, Pi-hole v6, or a public resolver).

findings.title: IPv6 is not provisioned on this network
findings.detail: No global IPv6 address and no IPv6 default route. The network runs IPv4-only; this is not an error by itself.
findings.recommendation: If your ISP offers IPv6, enable it on the router WAN (usually DHCPv6 with prefix delegation) and on the LAN (SLAAC/RA). On UniFi: Network → Internet → IPv6 = DHCPv6 + Prefix Delegation, then LAN networks → IPv6 Interface Type = Prefix Delegation.

findings.title: Some checks could not run or reach a conclusion
findings.detail: These parts of the network were not fully tested. Treat the absence of findings in these areas as 'unknown', not 'healthy'.
evidence: 6 IPv6 public-resolver addresses skipped (no working IPv6)
ping / packet-loss tests: ping command not available
path MTU (IPv4): ping command not available
traceroute disabled by option
Low Data Mode: 1 website sample per address family, response bodies capped at 512 KiB, scan HTTP budget 10 MiB — website timing confidence reduced
OS-path lookups on Linux/BSD use Go's resolver (resolv.conf + hosts), not glibc nsswitch modules such as mdns or nss-resolve
findings.recommendation: Install the missing tools (ping, traceroute) or re-run with both address families to close the gaps.

findings.title: DNSSEC validation could not be determined for System DNS #1 (Google Public DNS) (8.8.8.8:53)
findings.detail: The evidence was missing or contradictory (see the DNSSEC test detail). A SERVFAIL on its own is not treated as proof of validation.
evidence: DNSSEC validation @ 8.8.8.8:53 — INFO: the signed control domain did not resolve, so validation cannot be judged [signed control: NXDOMAIN; bogus zone: NXDOMAIN; bogus zone with CD=1: no answer (timeout)]

findings.title: DNSSEC validation could not be determined for System DNS #2 (Google Public DNS) (8.8.4.4:53)

evidence: DNSSEC validation @ 8.8.4.4:53 — INFO: the signed control domain did not resolve, so validation cannot be judged [signed control: NXDOMAIN; bogus zone: NXDOMAIN; bogus zone with CD=1: NXDOMAIN]

findings.title: Default gateway 192.0.2.1:53 does not answer DNS
findings.detail: The router does not run a DNS forwarder on this address (or blocks it). This is only a problem if you expect clients to use the router for DNS.
evidence: UDP/53 query (A example.com) @ 192.0.2.1:53 — FAIL: no response over UDP/53 (refused) [refused: read udp 192.0.2.2:52619->192.0.2.1:53: read: connection refused]

findings.title: Your network signals devices not to bypass its DNS
findings.detail: Canary domains are answered negatively, so browsers/OSes keep using this resolver instead of their own encrypted DNS or relay. Typical for Pi-hole, AdGuard Home, UniFi content filtering and parental controls.
evidence: Firefox auto-DoH disabled by: System DNS #1 (Google Public DNS) (8.8.8.8:53)
iCloud Private Relay blocked by: System DNS #1 (Google Public DNS) (8.8.8.8:53), System DNS #2 (Google Public DNS) (8.8.4.4:53)
findings.recommendation: Expected if you filter DNS; otherwise check the resolver's blocklists.

findings.title: Local resolver has encrypted-DNS ports open
findings.detail: TCP 853 (DoT) or 443 (DoH or a web UI) answer on the resolver address.
evidence: System DNS #1 (Google Public DNS) (8.8.8.8:53): TCP [443]
System DNS #2 (Google Public DNS) (8.8.4.4:53): TCP [443]

findings.title: Some local names / reverse lookups do not resolve
findings.detail: Local hostname or reverse (PTR) lookups failed. Not a fault, but it makes logs and device lists show IPs instead of names, and some apps (SSH, SMB, printers) resolve slowly while waiting.
evidence: [lan-ip-1] (reverse lookup of this computer's IP (docker0)): no PTR record
192.0.2.1 (reverse lookup of the default gateway): no PTR record
vm (this computer's own name) → 127.0.0.1
findings.recommendation: Enable 'register DHCP hostnames in DNS' / local domain on the router (UniFi: Settings → Networks → Domain Name).
